title: The Sixteenth Scholarship
premise: Hazel Eriksen transfers to Marrowgate Academy, a school built atop the ruins of the town's first theater, where a century-old tradition—the Sixteen Scholarships—has quietly funded sixteen students every year through an audition no one questions. Paired with his nemesis, sharp-tongued Wren Okafor, for a semester project on local history, Hazel uncovers that this year's sixteenth scholarship has been quietly redirected to line the pockets of the school's founding family. As their reluctant partnership deepens into friendship and something more, Hazel and Wren rally the town's overlooked kids to reclaim the audition, culminating in a final performance where Hazel—terrified of being seen—takes the stage himself to expose the theft and win back the scholarship for everyone.
about_author: N. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former small-town drama teacher who spent a decade collecting the secret histories of old school buildings before turning them into fiction. They write stories about kids who find their people in the unlikeliest corners of institutional hallways.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On his first day at Marrowgate Academy, Hazel maps the social terrain like a survival exercise: keep quiet, excel quietly, transfer out in June. He notices the strange warmth of the floor near the auditorium but files it away. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness disguised as strategy.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Mr. Voss announces semester projects and pairs Hazel with Wren Okafor, the girl who publicly dismantled his presentation in September. Their first meeting in the library is pure friction—she thinks he's a coward, he thinks she's exhausting. Beat: resentment with an undercurrent of grudging curiosity.

chapters.title: Sixteen Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Researching in the town archive, Wren drags Hazel into the story of the Sixteen Scholarships, endowed in 1898 by theater magnate Augustin Marrow for 'sixteen voices, chosen by merit alone.' Hazel recognizes the plaque in the lobby lists only fifteen names this year. Beat: intrigue replacing hostility.

chapters.title: Warm Floors
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Investigating the auditorium's odd heat, they find bricked-over stage doors beneath the gym—the original Marrow Theater, demolished but never fully buried. Wren's excitement is infectious; Hazel catches himself laughing for the first time all year. Beat: the ice cracking.

chapters.title: The Missing Sixteenth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cross-referencing endowment records, Wren discovers the sixteenth scholarship's funds have flowed to 'administrative heritage costs' since 2019—money funneled to the Marrow family trust. Hazel wants to drop it; invisible people don't fight institutions. Beat: fear versus conscience.

chapters.title: Detention Economics
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Caught after hours in the archive, both earn detention, where they meet janitor Emory Vance, who performed in the last true audition class of 1998. Emory hints the auditions were rigged even then—for students whose families could donate. Beat: disillusionment deepening the stakes.

chapters.title: Wren's Audition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback woven in: Wren auditioned freshman year and lost to a donor's daughter despite a flawless performance. She's been angry ever since; the project is her revenge. Hazel realizes her cruelty toward him was armor. Beat: empathy replacing judgment.

chapters.title: Headmistress Bell
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The pair requests records from Headmistress Bell, who deflects with charm and warns them off 'conspiracy thinking.' That night Hazel finds his locker moved and his project folder rifled. Someone is watching. Beat: the institution showing teeth.

chapters.title: The Understudies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Word spreads; other scholarship-hopeless kids join them—Deacon the cellist, Priya the painter, twins Sam and Sasha the stagehands. In the basement beneath the gym, they hold their first secret meeting among the old theater bones. Beat: found family assembling.

chapters.title: What Augustin Built
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging into Augustin Marrow's will, Hazel finds a clause: if the sixteenth scholarship is ever withheld from a merit audition for three consecutive years, the entire endowment reverts to the town. The clock expired last spring. Beat: hope with a legal deadline.

chapters.title: Paperwork and Threats
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They draft a formal claim, but Bell counters: Wren's mother's job at the school hangs by a thread, and Hazel's transfer placement could be revoked. Both are offered quiet deals. Wren almost takes hers. Beat: love against duty, tested individually.

chapters.title: The Fight
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel accuses Wren of considering betrayal; Wren calls him out for hiding behind invisibility while others bleed. They don't speak for a week. The project stalls. Beat: the relationship's lowest point, each seeing their own flaw in the other.

chapters.title: Emory's Tape
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Emory gives Hazel a VHS of the 1998 audition—showing young Emory performing brilliantly and losing anyway, and a teenage Bell watching from the wings, crying. Bell wasn't always the enemy. Beat: compassion complicating the conflict.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in B Minor
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Hazel practicing a speech he'll never give in the empty auditorium. She sits down beside him; they apologize without ceremony and finish the claim together overnight. Beat: partnership restored, warmer than before.

chapters.title: Filing Day
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They file the reversion claim with the town council, backed by forty student signatures and Emory's testimony. Bell escalates: the final audition is moved up two weeks, hoping to legitimize fifteen scholarships before the ruling. Beat: the trap snapping shut—and the plan forming inside it.

chapters.title: Sixteen Voices
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The group decides: if there must be an audition, they'll flood it. Sixteen students enter—including Hazel, who hasn't performed since a childhood humiliation. Training montage in the buried theater, lit by work lights. Beat: courage kindling collectively.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Two days before auditions, the buried theater floods—a burst pipe no one believes is accidental—and Deacon's cello is damaged. Evidence points to facilities staff under pressure from above. The group wavers; Hazel refuses to. Beat: resolve hardened by injustice.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Audition day. One by one the sixteen perform—Priya paints live, the twins run lights, Wren sings, Deacon plays on a borrowed instrument. Then Hazel walks out, hands shaking, and instead of performing, reads Augustin Marrow's will aloud to a stunned auditorium. Beat: the climax's first strike.

chapters.title: Bell's Choice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Confronted publicly, Bell breaks—not with defiance but exhaustion—and produces her own copy of the diverted ledgers, admitting she inherited the scheme and lacked the spine to end it. The council rules: the endowment reverts, and the sixteenth scholarship is awarded by merit, effective immediately. Beat: catharsis through confession.

chapters.title: Sixteenth Chair
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The committee names sixteen recipients. Wren finally gets her scholarship; so does Deacon, Priya, the twins. Hazel is offered one and declines it, asking it go to next year's unknown kid instead. Bell resigns; Emory is asked to lead the new audition board. Beat: justice distributed generously.

chapters.title: Curtain Call
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the spring showcase, held partly in the restored lower theater, Hazel performs after all—a short monologue about a boy who learned to be seen. Wren watches from the wings, then joins him for the bow. Beat: joy earned, love acknowledged without fanfare.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Plaque
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, months later. A new brass plaque lists sixteen names, ending with 'and all voices yet unheard.' Hazel decides to stay at Marrowgate. Wren slips her hand into his as they walk past Locker 114, now just a locker. Beat: belonging, at last, as the new tradition begins.
